indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B4.1.3.2 Demonstrate an understanding of strategies for comparing, adding and subtracting fractions (same denominator, or one being a multiple of the others)
indicator.objective: Provide examples of where fractions are used

skills.description: Identify fractions used in real-life contexts like cooking, sharing, and measuring.
Read time on a clock using fractions (half past, quarter past, quarter to).
Interpret circle graphs showing fractions of a whole.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Not recognizing fractions in daily life.
Misinterpreting pie charts or circle graphs.

questions.stem: A recipe calls for half a cup of milk. Which fraction represents this amount?
If you share a loaf of bread equally among 4 friends, what fraction of the bread does each person get?
hints: One out of four equal parts.

questions.stem: When the minute hand is on the 6, what fraction of an hour has passed?
A quarter past 3 is the same as what fraction of the hour?
questions.explanation: A quarter past is 1/4 of an hour.

questions.stem: A circle graph shows 1/2 of the pupils like football. What fraction do not like football?
A seamstress needs 1/3 of a metre of cloth for a dress. What fraction of a metre is left if she starts with 1 metre?
A quarter to 5 is the same as how many minutes before 5 o'clock?
hints: Quarter to means 15 minutes to the hour.
questions.explanation: A quarter to 5 means 15 minutes before 5.

questions.stem: A circle graph shows 10 pupils like apples out of 40 pupils. What fraction of the pupils like apples?
A pie is cut into 8 slices. If 3 slices are eaten, what fraction is left?
If you buy half a crate of eggs, what fraction of the crate do you NOT have?
questions.explanation: You do not have the other 1/2.

questions.stem: Give an example of where you might use fractions when sharing food with your family.
hints: Think about sharing a pizza or a cake.
questions.explanation: For example, if a family shares a pie cut into 6 slices, each person might get 1/6.

criteria.description: Gives a clear example of sharing food.

questions.misconception: Using fractions incorrectly in the example.

questions.stem: If it is half past 2, how many minutes past 2 o'clock is it?
Draw a circle graph where 1/4 of the circle is red, and 1/2 is blue. What fraction is left?

criteria.description: Draws a circle divided into 4 parts.
Shades 1 part red and 2 parts blue.

questions.stem: If a bottle holds 1 litre of water, and you drink 3/4 of it, how much is left?
A pupil says 'I will be there in three-quarters of an hour'. How many minutes is that?
In a circle graph, the sector for 'Maths' is 1/3 of the circle, and 'English' is 1/4. What fraction represents the rest of the subjects?
questions.misconception: Adding the numerators and denominators directly (2/7).

questions.stem: Explain how you use fractions when measuring ingredients for a recipe.
hints: Have you ever used 1/2 a cup?
questions.explanation: When cooking, you often measure things like half a cup of sugar or a quarter teaspoon of salt. These are common fractions used in recipes.

criteria.description: Gives examples of fractions like 1/2 or 1/4.

questions.misconception: Thinking fractions are only used in math class.

questions.stem: A class has 40 pupils. A circle graph shows that 1/4 like Science, 1/2 like Maths, and the rest like English. How many pupils like English?
Explain the difference between 'quarter past' and 'quarter to' the hour.
questions.explanation: Quarter past is 15 minutes after the hour, while quarter to is 15 minutes before the next hour.

criteria.description: Explains quarter past is 15 minutes after.
Explains quarter to is 15 minutes before.

questions.misconception: Thinking they mean the same thing.

questions.stem: A carpenter has a piece of wood that is 2 metres long. He cuts off 1/2 a metre. How much wood is left? Express your answer as a fraction.
